title: A frame with a buffer
description:
Write `to_decimal(buffer, n)`: it writes the **signed** number n into the buffer as text with a 0 at the end (a minus sign for negative numbers), and returns the number of characters, not counting the 0.

Use a classic stack frame: `push rbp`, `mov rbp, rsp`, `sub rsp, 32` for a local buffer where you build the digits backwards, then copy them to the caller's buffer, and finish with `leave` and `ret`.

The most negative number, −9223372036854775808, has no positive twin: negating it gives itself. Divide it as an **unsigned** number after negating and it works.

starter.solution.asm:
to_decimal:
        mov     byte [rdi], 0
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
to_decimal:
        push    rbp
        mov     rbp, rsp
        sub     rsp, 32
        mov     rax, rsi
        xor     r9d, r9d                ; 1 when negative
        test    rax, rax
        jns     .digits
        mov     r9d, 1
        neg     rax                     ; the most negative stays itself, fine as unsigned
.digits:
        lea     r8, [rbp - 1]
        mov     ecx, 10
.digit: xor     edx, edx
        div     rcx
        add     dl, '0'
        mov     [r8], dl
        dec     r8
        test    rax, rax
        jnz     .digit
        test    r9d, r9d
        jz      .copy
        mov     byte [r8], '-'
        dec     r8
.copy:  inc     r8
        lea     rcx, [rbp]
        sub     rcx, r8                 ; the length
        mov     rax, rcx
        mov     rsi, r8
        rep movsb
        mov     byte [rdi], 0
        leave
        ret

rules: Start with the classic prologue: push rbp.
unitTests:
test "positive numbers"
    to_decimal(buf(32), 12345) => "12345"
    to_decimal(buf(32), 7) => "7"
    to_decimal(buf(32), 0) => "0"
test "negative numbers"
    to_decimal(buf(32), -42) => "-42"
    to_decimal(buf(32), -1) => "-1"
test "the extremes"
    to_decimal(buf(32), 9223372036854775807) => "9223372036854775807"
    to_decimal(buf(32), -9223372036854775808) => "-9223372036854775808"
test "the length"
    to_decimal(buf(32), 12345) == 5
    to_decimal(buf(32), -42) == 3
    to_decimal(buf(32), -9223372036854775808) == 20
